name: Tiria
overview: Tiria is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Jehallelel. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes or narrative details provided. His role is preserved in the biblical record to establish lineage within the tribe of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Tiria appears as a proper name in Scripture without an accompanying meaning or divine attribution. It is recorded plainly in 1 Chronicles 4:16, serving as a straightforward identifier rather than conveying specific theological significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Tiria as the son of Jehallelel, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no further family connections or relationships are documented for Tiria in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tiria's significance lies in his inclusion in the genealogical records of the tribe of Judah, which underscores the importance of preserving God-ordained lineage among His people. While the biblical narrative does not elaborate on his personal deeds or character, his mention contributes to the broader biblical emphasis on heritage and God's faithfulness to His covenant through successive generations.
